name: Klaus-Dieter Richter
bio:
Klaus-Dieter's journey into motorsport began unconventionally, not with a racing family or a go-karting obsession, but with a fascination for fluid dynamics. He devoured textbooks on aerodynamics and spent countless hours in his youth building model airplanes, meticulously testing wing designs in a makeshift wind tunnel in his garage. This dedication led him to a degree in aerospace engineering, followed by a stint at a major automotive manufacturer, where he honed his skills in computational fluid dynamics. 

His true calling, however, remained in racing. He joined a smaller Formula team initially, quickly proving his worth with innovative aerodynamic solutions that squeezed out crucial tenths of a second. Klaus-Dieter is known for his methodical and data-driven approach. He is a firm believer that success lies in the details. He joined Lechner Racing five years ago, and his leadership has been instrumental in the team's improved aerodynamic performance. 

He has a reputation for being demanding but fair, pushing his team to constantly improve and explore new ideas, while maintaining a focus on reliability and proven concepts. His meticulous nature, combined with his innovative thinking, makes him a valuable asset to any racing team.

physical.hairStyle: short, neatly combed to the side with a slight receding hairline
physical.description: Klaus-Dieter is a man of medium build with a serious demeanor.

quirks: Always carries a worn copy of 'Aerodynamic Theory' by Hoerner.
Insists on calibrating the wind tunnel himself, even for minor adjustments.
Has a particular dislike for poorly designed winglets and will openly criticize them.
